unmapped_findings: [b0024] For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl system, alloys with 2–6 wt.% Al have mechanical properties falling between the values of the Al-free alloy and the 8 wt.% Al alloy; aging has a much smaller influence on the tensile behavior in the 2–6 wt.% Al cases. This applies to the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al sample but is not specific to the 450 °C/24 h condition.

[figure_004] In the tensile-strength vs elongation summary, the 2Al (pale cyan) points form the lowest-strength clusters at roughly 460–600 MPa with elongation spanning ~8% to ~55%; this is aggregated across all aging conditions for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al alloy and is not specific to the 450 °C/24 h condition.

[figure_003] For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy family, YS stays between roughly 350 and 450 MPa from 0Al to 4Al; UTS passes through a minimum near 2Al; TE drops to a minimum at 2Al; hardness is nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al. These are alloy-level trends, not specific numerical values for the 450 °C/24 h, 2Al sample.

[b0031] For compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al, the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism, so dislocation-based strain hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning is the primary strain-hardening mechanism; this applies to the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al sample (30 wt.% Mn, 2 wt.% Al).

[b0025] The intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared with the ~8 wt.% Al variant; the pronounced strengthening is attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides mainly in the 8Al case, while the 2–6 wt.% Al cases show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior.
